explanation: Walk out to a turning point at x = A and back again, and watch the two quantities split. Distance is the whole path length you covered — it only ever grows. Displacement is the straight arrow from where you started to where you are now; on the way back it shrinks, and after a full round trip it returns to zero even though you walked 2A.
bullets: Distance is a scalar: the total length of the path actually travelled.
Displacement is a vector: straight-line change in position, start to finish.
On a round trip distance = 2A but displacement = 0 — they are not the same.
